QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_7

question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund delivered annualised return of 18% over 3 years with Maximum Drawdown of 12%. What is the Calmar Ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: The Calmar Ratio is defined as Annualised Return divided by the absolute value of Maximum Drawdown over the same period: Calmar = 18% / 12% = 1.50. It is a return-per-unit-of-drawdown-risk measure widely used for trend-following and managed-futures strategies, where drawdown management is a core selling point. Higher Calmar values indicate better return per unit of historical pain. The Trap: 0.67 inverts the ratio (MDD / return). 2.16 reflects using a cumulative (non-annualised) return in the numerator. 1.06 introduces an extraneous risk-free-rate adjustment that is not part of the Calmar definition. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (164, 173, 174, 175, 231) support MDD and return metrics but do not define the Calmar Ratio or provide the Annualised Return / MDD formula. The definition and framing above are general industry/quantitative-finance knowledge rather than a workbook-page citation.
